forecaster_note: Best energy of the week is on the table right now — a 4.3ft E swell at 10 seconds is pushing 208 kJ into the Northern Beaches, and the 96° angle is close enough to the ENE window that Dee Why and Long Reef are both loading up properly rather than closing out. Winds are dead glassy at dawn (1–2 kph WSW offshore) and don't turn ENE until around midday, so the clean window is early. It's a one-day spike: by Thursday energy collapses to 37 kJ with lovely NW offshores over thigh-to-stomach leftovers, and Saturday is knee-high junk at 8 kJ. Sunday rebuilds to 38–56 kJ but the bulk of it arrives from 187° — dead south, which wraps badly into Dee Why. If you can only get wet once this week, it's this morning. (Agent-generated summary from Surfline forecast data — Surfline's own forecaster paragraph was not available this run.)

wind.summary: Glassy WSW offshore at dawn, swinging ENE onshore ~10 kph from midday

days.label: Today
days.note: The pick of the week. 208 kJ of E swell at 10 seconds with a glassy WSW offshore until roughly midday — go early, the ENE seabreeze puts a lid on it from noon. Low tide 6:10am filling to a 1.4m high at 12:52pm, so the Point improves as the tide pushes.

dee-why.window: 7:30–11:00am. Dead glassy WSW offshore, tide pushing off the 6:10am low into the Point.

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: 208 kJ is more than triple what you'll see tomorrow, and at 96° the E swell is wrapping into the Point instead of dumping on the bank. That's your frontside right — sit wide and let the 10-second sets do the work rather than chasing the shorter SSE lumps.

long-reef.window: Dawn–10:30am. Biggest of the four on this angle; wind goes cross by noon.

tip.label: Biggest option today
tip.text: Long Reef is the swell magnet on an E angle — Surfline has it chest-to-overhead on the same 208 kJ everyone else is getting at waist-to-shoulder. If you want the solid 4–5ft-with-shape session you like, this is the one, but it's a paddle.

curl-curl.window: 7:00–11:00am before the ENE fills in. Punchier, shorter-period banks.

tip.label: Punchy beachie option
tip.text: Straight E swell into open beach means shifting peaks and closeout risk on the sets — but this is exactly the punchy 3–4ft beachie shape you rate. Pick a bank early and stay on it; it gets messy fast once the ENE arrives.

manly.window: Early only — the ENE goes straight onshore at North Steyne from midday.
alerts: Wind turns onshore at Manly earlier than the northern spots

tip.label: Skip unless you're already south
tip.text: Same 208 kJ but the least favourable exposure today, and Manly is the first of the four to cop the ENE onshore. Dee Why or Long Reef are a better use of the same drive.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Energy craters from 208 to 37 kJ overnight — small, but genuinely clean. NW–NNW offshore holds all morning and only goes light N by midday, so it's a groom-your-technique session rather than a power session.

dee-why.window: 9:00am–12:00pm. NNW offshore at 3 kph — glassy, small, forgiving.

tip.label: Volume day
tip.text: 37 kJ is a fifth of today's energy. Nothing in the quiver that needs a wave to push it will work — this is a paddle-and-flow session, and the clean NNW offshore makes it worth going anyway.

long-reef.window: Mid-morning. Holds the most size of the four again, offshore through noon.

manly.window: Early. Smallest of the four and the wind goes cross by 9am.
alerts: Smallest spot on the coast tomorrow

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is a write-off — knee-to-thigh at 8 kJ, the flattest day on the chart. Sunday is the weekend session: energy rebuilds to 38–56 kJ, but the primary is 2.3ft at 9s from 187°, which is dead south and wraps badly into Dee Why. NW offshore until roughly 11am, then ENE onshore. Long Reef and Curl Curl handle the S angle better.

alerts: Sat 22: knee-to-thigh at 8 kJ — not worth the drive
Sun 23: 187° swell is dead south and wraps poorly here

long-reef.window: Sunday 8:00–11:30am — best of the four on the S angle, wind stays cross rather than onshore.

curl-curl.window: Sunday morning. NW offshore to ~11am, then ENE puts a lid on it.

manly.window: Sunday early only — wind goes cross by 9am and onshore by noon.
alerts: Weakest of the four both days
